was a high heterogeneity among the studies analyzed (overall: I2 ¼ 93%). Which can be mainly attributed to vitamin E trials
(I2 ¼ 96%) as no signiﬁcant heterogeneity effect was observed in vitamin C trials. In fact, one particular vitamin E trial (Boshtam
et al., 2002) which reported a huge hypotensive effect.
Regarding diastolic blood pressure (Fig. 6) we found a similar overall hypotensive effect induced by vitamin treatment (MD
2.06) [95% CI 3.29, 0.83; p ¼ 0.001] in 30 clinical trials (n ¼ 1537). However, when analyzing each supplementation on
its own, no effects were observed for vitamin C (p ¼ 0.06), vitamin E (p ¼ 0.05) and vitamin E þ C (p ¼ 0.05). It is important
to note that the length of the supplementation was not a source of heterogeneity neither for systolic nor for diastolic blood pressure
as showed by the meta-regression model.
